questions.question: The interior angles of any quadrilateral sum to:
questions.rationale: A diagonal splits a quadrilateral into 2 triangles: 2 × 180° = 360°, matching the formula (n − 2) × 180° for n = 4.

questions.question: What is the sum of the interior angles of a hexagon?
questions.rationale: (6 − 2) × 180° = 720°. From one vertex, a hexagon divides into 4 triangles.

questions.question: The sum of the exterior angles (one at each vertex) of any polygon is:
options: Depends on the number of sides
questions.rationale: Walking once around the polygon, you turn a full 360° in total, regardless of how many sides it has.

questions.question: Each interior angle of a regular pentagon measures:
Which property belongs to a rhombus but NOT to every parallelogram?
questions.rationale: Every rhombus has perpendicular diagonals, while a general parallelogram (e.g. a slanted rectangle) does not.

questions.question: A square can be described as:
options: A rectangle with all sides equal
Both a rectangle and a rhombus
questions.rationale: A square sits at the junction of the rectangle and rhombus branches — it inherits every property of both.

questions.question: The diagonals of a rectangle are always:
options: Equal in length and bisect each other
questions.rationale: Rectangle diagonals are equal and bisect each other; perpendicularity belongs to rhombi and angle-bisecting to rhombi/squares.

questions.question: A rhombus has diagonals 10 cm and 8 cm. Its area is:
questions.rationale: Rhombus area = ½ × d₁ × d₂ = ½ × 10 × 8 = 40 cm².

questions.question: Joining the midpoints of the sides of ANY quadrilateral in order always produces a:
questions.rationale: Varignon's theorem: the midpoint quadrilateral is always a parallelogram whose sides are parallel to the original diagonals.
